rootCause.shape: the pinned SCSS grammar produces ONE `ERROR` node with **15,479 named children** for this file (2,508 `$`-variable declarations). The analyzer descends into ERROR regions ON PURPOSE (that descent was itself an earlier fix — error recovery is required by the lane's fixtures), so it walks that node's whole child list.
rootCause.cost: `namedChild(i)` measured at 176 us/call at 1,000 lines and 312 us/call at 2,000 lines; 2,619 calls >0.5 ms on that single ERROR node accounted for 5.8 s of a 9.6 s analysis. The wall clock grows superlinearly while the OUTPUT stays constant at 30 symbols.
rootCause.shared: the CSS delegate walks the same ERROR node and is a large share of the remaining cost (CSS alone: 0.93 s @1,000 lines · 3.77 s @2,000 · 38.0 s @4,000).

ownerIndex.what: `ownerForNode` scanned EVERY symbol per call; replaced with a pruned interval index (sorted by span start + prefix max end, with an identity guard for the `unshift`-ed module symbol).
ownerIndex.result: CPU-time A/B, alternating arms (load-independent): 1.01x / 1.04x on the pathological file, and 1.19x (derived-variables) · 1.14x (bootstrap _variables, 558 symbols) · 1.16x (initial-variables) · 1.05x (element-plus var.scss) on ordinary symbol-bearing files.
ownerIndex.equivalence: 111/111 sampled files byte-identical output (sha256 digest of every symbol and relationship), re-verified after the narrowing fix.

cursorWalkSwap.what: replacing `for (i < namedChildCount) namedChild(i)` with `for (c = firstNamedChild; c; c = c.nextNamedSibling)` in the 9 indexed walks.
cursorWalkSwap.result: CPU-time A/B: **0.88x at 1,000 lines and 0.80x at 2,000 lines — a REGRESSION** (4,845 ms original vs 6,066 ms swapped at 2,000).
cursorWalkSwap.verdict: REVERTED, and this is the load-bearing negative result: the idiom swap is NOT the fix, so it must not be proposed for the CSS analyzer either. The per-call cost is not index scanning; the cursor idiom's own per-step overhead is worse on these trees.

gateBeforeAfter.difference: +37 edges (references +8, exports +29), +26 resolved, +11 amb(decl); extFAIL/bindFAIL/causeFAIL remain 0; the HOLE clause is UNSTATED on the after run rather than absent.
gateBeforeAfter.theControlThatMissedIt: CLOSED TWICE, and the SECOND closure REFUTES the first. First I attributed the +37 to my owner index (arms run ~9 minutes apart, original 9,358/4,048 vs index 9,350/4,019). Then two stronger controls were run: (1) a SAME-PROCESS comparison of both analyzers over ALL 4,433 admitted files, diffing every symbol and every edge key — **0 files differ, 0 symbols or edges present with one analyzer only**; (2) three whole-population enumeration runs (index, original, index) — **all three read references 9,350 · exports 4,019**. So the owner index is OUTPUT-NEUTRAL: the 37-edge difference was the TREE MOVING between arms, not the change, and my first attribution was itself the artifact this section was written to guard against. SAMPLE-SCOPED equivalence was the weaker claim I originally made; POPULATION-SCOPED neutrality is the claim two independent controls now support, and the +37 is neither dedupe nor members lost — it is a transient state of the tree.
gateBeforeAfter.whatIsAttributable: the +37 reproduces in the cause enumeration (references 9,358, exports 4,048 — the SAME numbers as the after-gate), and that enumeration ran with this lane's analyzer; the before-gate ran with the pre-change analyzer. So the difference is consistent with this lane's change, and it is NOT separately controlled against another lane's shared-file edits in the same window (css/engine are shared and were not touched by me). Named rather than assumed either way.
gateBeforeAfter.howToSettleIt: one same-revision A/B: revert the owner index in a scratch module and run the gate row for references/exports — or run the 111-file harness WITHOUT the size cap and with a stride that covers these files.

attempt2.what: a TARGETED variant: use the sibling walk only where `namedChildCount > 64` (the wide recovery node), keep the indexed walk everywhere else — written to avoid the per-step penalty that sank the global swap.
attempt2.result: CPU-time A/B, alternating arms, same input: **0.56x at 1,000 lines and 0.84x at 2,000** — slower, so REVERTED. The file is byte-identical to the committed state (sha256 e2400903efb4ffca).
attempt2.whatItRefutes: the reading that `namedChild(i)`'s cost growth (176 us/call at 1,000 lines, 312 us/call at 2,000) is INDEX SCANNING. `nextNamedSibling` walking is slower even on the wide node, so the per-call cost is not a function of the index — it is per-node access cost itself (marshalling/allocation/GC), which grows with the tree.

idiomFixesRefuted.bothIdiomsRefuted: global cursor swap 0.80x · wide-node cursor path 0.56-0.84x. The iteration idiom is NOT the lever, and a fleet-wide 'fix' on it would have cost every lane.
whatRemains: REDUCE THE NUMBER OF NODE ACCESSES — the one lever neither attempt touched. That means NOT descending into a 15k-child ERROR region, which is a SEMANTIC trade (recovery completeness for speed) and belongs to the lane owner and the Lead, not to an optimisation pass: the descent exists because refusing it once made every read inside a broken region invisible, and a fixture pins that behaviour.

OR the shared delegate's per-node cost on the same region: this lane's share of the hole is ~68% at the 2,000-line prefix (7.8 s of 11.5 s total, CSS delegate 3.7 s), so neither side alone explains it and both are node-access bound.
PRICED BUT UNMEASURED: capping the recovery descent at a child-count threshold. It would need its own before/after AND the 13 fixtures re-run, because it changes what is recovered.

boundedDescent.ruled: Lead: the alternative to a bounded descent on the pathological node is not full recovery, it is TOTAL LOSS.
boundedDescent.where: BOTH layers, because the profile said the remainder was the shared delegate's: `src/ast/real-scss-analyzer.ts` and `src/ast/real-css-analyzer.ts` (the second was Lead-authorized, css being a verified lane).
boundedDescent.channelCorrection: The disclosure was first attached to the file's MODULE SYMBOL on the reasoning that analyzer-internal tallies do not survive `parseFile` but a symbol's metadata does. THAT WAS WRONG, and measured wrong: `parseFile` strips symbol metadata COMPLETELY — on the pathological file every symbol arrives with no metadata keys at all (`[...new Set(symbols.flatMap(s => Object.keys(s.metadata)))]` is `[]`). What survives is RELATIONSHIP metadata, the channel the fleet's own markers ride, so the tally now rides the file's first relationship.
